ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, terminal a is connected by a wire to the upper vertex; terminal b is connected by a wire to the lower-right node. Between the lower-right node and the central black dot is an ordinary wire, so they belong to the same potential node. From the upper vertex to the central black dot there is a 6Ω resistor, and from the upper vertex to the lower-right node there is also a 6Ω resistor. From the lower-left node to the central black dot there is a 4Ω resistor, and from the lower-left node to the lower-right node there is a 4Ω resistor. From the upper vertex to the lower-left node there is also a 4Ω resistor. Reasoning: First merge the central black dot with the node where terminal b is located. In this way, from the upper vertex, namely terminal a, to b there are two direct 6Ω branches, and they are in parallel. From the lower-left node to b there are two 4Ω resistors in parallel, equivalent to 4Ω || 4Ω = 2Ω; then in series with the 4Ω from a to the lower-left node, forming an a-to-b branch of 4Ω + 2Ω = 6Ω. Therefore the whole network is equivalent to three 6Ω branches in parallel: Req = 6Ω || 6Ω || 6Ω = 2Ω.

Also the two 4Ω resistors from the lower-left node to b are in parallel, giving 2Ω, and this is in series with the 4Ω resistor from a to the lower-left node, giving a third a-to-b branch of 6Ω. Thus the network becomes three 6Ω branches in parallel, so the equivalent resistance is 2Ω.

method.method_draft: Apply a convenient test voltage, e.g. set Va = 1 V and Vb = 0 V, with the center node also at 0 V because it is wired to b. Let the lower-left node voltage be Vx. KCL at the lower-left node gives (Vx-1)/4 + Vx/4 + Vx/4 = 0, so Vx = 1/3 V. The current drawn from terminal a is through two 6Ω resistors directly to b plus the 4Ω resistor to the lower-left node: I = 1/6 + 1/6 + (1 - 1/3)/4 = 1/2 A. Therefore Req = V/I = 1/(1/2) = 2Ω.
